# (PART\*) Complete workflow: Lagoa do Sino {-}

# Data, areas and maps {#lagoa-areas}

In this part, every analysis in the package is applied, one after another, to a
12.5 km² hexagon centred on the UFSCar Lagoa do Sino campus in Buri, São Paulo,
using the MapBiomas Collection 10 annual maps from 1985 to 2024. The maps object
ships with the package (it is stored under the name `mapas`):

```{r}
load(system.file("examples", "mapa_exemplo.Rdata", package = "biomastats"))
maps <- mapas
```

## Area by class {-}

`get_area()` measures the area of each class in each year, accounting for the
true area of every pixel, and returns both the table (`aggregate_data`) and a
plot of the series:

```{r areas, fig.height=5.5}
areas <- get_area(maps, plot_type = "areaplot")
areas$time_series
```

```{r include=FALSE}
a <- areas$aggregate_data
km2 <- function(code, year) sum(a$area_raw[a$land_class == code & a$year == year])
total85 <- sum(a$area_raw[a$year == 1985])
pas85 <- km2(15, 1985); pas24 <- km2(15, 2024)
soy85 <- km2(39, 1985); soy24 <- km2(39, 2024)
for85 <- km2(3, 1985); for24 <- km2(3, 2024)
```

In four decades, the landscape switched its productive base. In 1985, pasture
covered `r num(pas85)` km², `r num(100 * pas85 / total85, 0)`% of the area; by
2024, only `r num(pas24)` km² remained. Over the same period, soybean, absent in
1985, grew to `r num(soy24)` km² and came to dominate the landscape. Forest
formation shrank from `r num(100 * for85, 0)` ha to `r num(100 * for24, 0)` ha, a
loss of `r num(100 * (for85 - for24) / for85, 0)`%.

## Maps {-}

With `land_vis()`, this transformation shows up on the map of each year, with
the official MapBiomas legend and colours:

```{r maps, fig.show="hold", out.width="50%", fig.width=6, fig.height=6}
land_vis(maps, year = 1985)
land_vis(maps, year = 2024)
```

## Composition in one year {-}

To summarise the composition of a single year, `land_dist()` draws a bar chart
(`type = "barplot"`) or a pie chart (`type = "pie"`):

```{r distribution, fig.height=4.5}
land_dist(areas, year = 2024, type = "barplot")
```
